OpenECS-std 0.4.0 runs on Windows: every standard plugin builds and passes its tests there. gpu gives a text's glyphs to your own shaders, so a 3D scene can have labels.

It comes out with [OpenECS 0.4.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS/releases/tag/v0.4.0), which ships these plugins built, in its `plugins/` folder, for Linux and now Windows. The [examples of OpenECS-examples 0.4.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-examples/releases/tag/v0.4.0) use them.

## What you can do

**Use the standard plugins on Windows.** They build with LLVM-MinGW or MinGW's gcc, on Windows or as a cross compiler from Linux, and the checks run the examples' tests on Windows.

- net and web check servers against Windows' trusted root certificates. A file of certificates, such as the one `SSL_CERT_FILE` names, still comes first.
- fs watches folders on Windows by reading each watched folder again every half second. It tells what was added, removed, or changed in size or time, as on Linux.

**Label a 3D scene.** `gpu.glyphs(font, text, size)` gives the glyphs of a text for your own pipeline. It gives the text's width and line height, and for each texture that holds some of its glyphs, the texture's number, the glyphs' rectangles as vertices, and their indices. A draw with `atlas` set to that number samples the texture.

## Small fixes

- A plugin's `header.h`, such as ui's C macros, reaches its definition header on Windows too.
- Build errors show in the same style as the rest of the build's lines.

## What will break

Nothing that plugins use changes.

## Downloads

- `openecs-std-0.4.0-source.tar.gz`: the source with the libraries it compiles in. Build it inside a checkout of OpenECS, as README.md says.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the checksum of the archive.

The standard plugins are under the zlib license. The libraries in `dependencies/` keep their own licenses, which OpenECS's release lists.
